macro.event: Fed Chair Kevin Warsh - Jackson Hole keynote (livestreamed)
macro.note: His first as Chair. DOUBLE-CONFIRMED on two primary calendars, with a title conflict noted rather than reconciled: the Kansas City Fed program titles the slot Opening Remarks, the Federal Reserve Board calendar says Keynote Remarks. 8:00 a.m. Mountain, Kristin Forbes of MIT chairing, streamed on youtube.com/kansascityfed - and only the Chair's address is streamed. Symposium theme: Financial Innovation, Implications for Payments and Policy. BofA's Mark Cabana is the sharpest stated risk: a structural rather than cyclical speech would read dovish and could push the 30Y toward 5.5%. Note what the volatility market has priced for this: VXN closed at a seven-month low

macro.event: BLS preliminary payroll benchmark revision (CES, March 2026) and QCEW Q1
macro.note: BLS schedule-confirmed, National plus State and Area, landing at the SAME MINUTE as the Chair. This is the least-watched high-consequence number of the month: last year's preliminary benchmark revision was a downward revision of 911,000 jobs and it reset the entire labour-market debate. Monthly CES estimates are NOT revised today - the benchmark is applied with the January reference period in February. With July payrolls already at MINUS 23,000 and a 4.1% unemployment rate, a large downward revision would be the strongest argument yet against the hawks

Confirmed from the Surveys of Consumers' own site. The preliminary read was 51.0, with Current Conditions 51.8 and Expectations 50.6, against a July final of 55.2 - a collapse of more than four points in the headline. No named-poll consensus exists for a final revision, so none is asserted here. For the record, an aggregator carrying an actual of 51.0 is recycling the preliminary

macro.note: Dallas Fed-confirmed. July production was 10.1. Month-end index rebalancing and settlement flows sit alongside it, which is worth knowing before reading Monday's tape as information

macro.note: July ISM manufacturing was 55.6% and June JOLTS openings 7.4mn, both from the issuing agencies. Construction spending the same morning. First hard data of September, two weeks before the Sept 15-16 FOMC

macro.event: Beige Book; ADP employment and factory orders earlier
macro.note: Fed and ADP confirmed. July ADP was plus 44,000. The Beige Book is the last qualitative read the committee publishes before the September meeting

BLS-confirmed. July was MINUS 23,000 payrolls with unemployment at 4.1%. This is the single most consequential number between today and the Sept 15-16 FOMC, and it lands one week from today. Waller speaks Thursday 9/3 at 8:30, with claims, ISM services (July 54.1%) and the trade balance the same day
